Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The context describes the Flote as a wind instrument designed for people with limited mobility, focusing on accessibility and cost-effectiveness. The primary utilitarian mechanic (head movement and breath control) was designed first to ensure the instrument's functionality and accessibility. The design process emphasizes utility first, with the goal of creating an instrument that is both playable and affordable.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The Flote has two performance modes, which are selected using a checkbox labeled “mode” via the control panel on the user interface. In the default mode (“unlocked”), the player's movements directly change the pitch of the instrument. In locked mode, once a note has been begun, the player is free to move without changing the pitch. This indicates a flexible structure with rules.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The Flote is described as a musical instrument that relies on the player's head movements and breath control to produce notes. The instrument is designed to be expressive and allows for creative expression, which suggests a skill-based activity. The calibration process and the customization of the tracking system to match the player's abilities further indicate that the instrument requires skill to play effectively. The absence of any mention of chance or random elements in the instrument's design supports the conclusion that it is entirely skill-based.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The Flote allows the player to move their head and blow into a microphone to produce notes. There are no turns or phases described, and the actions of moving the head and blowing into the microphone can be done simultaneously. The 'locked' mode still allows for simultaneous actions, as the player can move to prepare for the next note while still playing the current note.
